keys.statement: Prefer an entrainer that forms two liquid phases with the mixture, so a decanter separates and returns it; homogeneous azeotropic distillation recirculates more azeotrope and uses more energy.

decisions.mechanism: Liquid-liquid splitting in a decanter does part of the separation without heat.
decisions.operation: Choose a heterogeneous entrainer with a decanter.

keys.statement: Removing water azeotropically during esterification shortens the reaction and raises conversion; a cited isoamyl acetate study reports 2.7% higher conversion than ordinary water separation.

decisions.mechanism: Azeotropic removal takes water out as it forms.
decisions.operation: Couple esterification with azeotropic water removal.

keys.statement: In a cited acetic acid dehydration process, a partial condenser between the column top and the decanter stopped azeotrope building up in the column and cut energy use.

decisions.obstacle: Azeotrope accumulating in an azeotropic dehydration column.
decisions.mechanism: Part of the overhead is condensed and handled before the decanter.
decisions.operation: Add a partial condenser ahead of the decanter.
